about: Real captures used on the marketing site: the Galley app (public/screens/ showcase, public/docs/ the docs pages' pictures, public/howto/ the how-to steps) and the Caddow example site itself (public/sites/). Every one comes from scripts/capture-screens.mjs, run against the released Galley (galley-cms 0.2.0 from npm) with a throwaway home, throwaway copies of the fashion starter (Caddow) and the small-business starter (Lowfield, the target of the WordPress move), a stand-in Cloudflare and a stand-in WordPress site. 1440 × 900 window at 2× device scale, light theme, WebP only, with a 1× copy (<name>@1x.webp). Showcase and how-to pictures are kept under about 160 KB (quality is lowered before anything is shrunk); docs pictures keep the exact size their page declares and stay under 120 KB.
setup: Everything is in scripts/capture/: README.md has the exact steps; start.sh starts each part with a clean environment and a throwaway home (sites, host, wordpress, hosting, galley, hosted, stop); serve-host.mts is the stand-in Cloudflare for putting the site online.
sh scripts/capture/start.sh sites — the two throwaway sites, made with the released CLI; versions are published as Tobiah Rusk <tobiah@caddow.example>, an invented person from the starter.
sh scripts/capture/start.sh host — the stand-in Cloudflare on 4791 (made-up account, caddow.example-studio.workers.dev, the zone caddow.example); prints the key it accepts.
sh scripts/capture/start.sh wordpress — the importer's stand-in WordPress site on 4792 (Fernhill Garden Studio: 12 posts, 6 pages, 2 built with Elementor).

sh scripts/capture/start.sh hosting — the stand-in Fly.io and Cloudflare for "Host the editor online" (scripts/rehearse-hosting.mjs on 4793/4794, a fake install on 4796); writes the variables the app needs to hosting.env.

ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=… sh scripts/capture/start.sh galley — the released Galley on 4790, open on Caddow, pointed at the stand-ins; the key comes from the shell of whoever runs it and goes to that process only.
HOSTED_PASSWORD=… sh scripts/capture/start.sh hosted — a hosted install (galley serve, no site) at http://cms.localhost:4797, for its sign-in and first run.
Open Lowfield too (POST /api/sites/open), read both ids (GET /api/sites); the token is in the Open: line of the Galley log.
command: GALLEY_ORIGIN=http://127.0.0.1:4790 GALLEY_TOKEN=<token> GALLEY_SITE=<Caddow id> SITE_DIR=<capture dir>/home/sites/caddow WP_SITE=<Lowfield id> WP_URL=http://127.0.0.1:4792 CF_KEY=<stand-in key> HOSTED_URL=http://cms.localhost:4797 HOSTED_PASSWORD=<the throwaway password> PLAYWRIGHT_MODULES=<node_modules with playwright-core> node scripts/capture-screens.mjs   (no step names = the whole session in order, about an hour)
captured: 2026-11-24, Galley 0.2.0 (the published package), the whole set in one session following scripts/capture/README.md. Assistant spend: $0.48 as the app reports it (the brand read, two edits, the Publish window's note).

Media: the site's photographs with sizes, filters, Upload, Generate a video and Generate an image.
Forms: the three forms, where their submissions go, their fields, and the note about where the live site should send submissions.

Inbox: Write to the workroom with three submissions — two from invented visitors (sent from another local address, so not marked Test) and the inbox's own test — one (Corin Vale, a repair) open with every answer and where it was sent from.
Scripts: Plausible (off) and Google Analytics 4 (on, consent: Analytics) installed; the built-in consent banner's words on the right.
Search & AI: 1 must fix, 1 should fix, 2 ideas; the groups with their marks; How AI systems see this site.
Search & AI scrolled to the AI crawlers panel: OpenAI's training crawler blocked, the rest allowed, an Allow/Block switch for each.
Redirects: the list of 8 (one, /winter-sale/ → /sale/, marked as leading nowhere), Where they take effect: Cloudflare, Try an address.
Add many redirects with eleven pasted lines: the review catching a loop (in red), an address not on the site and a duplicate.
Try an address answering /about-us/ → /atelier/ (Ends on “The atelier”), and Health: 1 leads nowhere.
Site settings: Addresses (live and staging) and Online.
The brand proposal read from Caddow: Nothing is saved yet / Save the brand, Worth a look, the first colours marked Measured or Declared.
The proposal's Type part.
The proposal's Voice part, written by the assistant from the site's words.
The Material part with a PDF of brand notes, the wordmark and a note added.
The editor: the home page's form beside the preview, Campaign hero open with its 2 edits (Heading Edited, Put back).
The Pieces heading retyped in place on the page (“Coats and knits to start with”).
The assistant's real reply after changing the campaign heading and first button, with Review in Proof and Undo this change, beside the page showing “Coats for low sun.”
Proof › What changed for the home page: the campaign heading and button (by the assistant) and the Pieces heading (on the page), each with Put back.
Proof › Source: the same changes as lines of src/content/pages/index.md.
The Publish 3 changes? window over Proof: the suggested note, What goes (three pages), Recorded as Tobiah Rusk.
Version history after that publish: the newest version (Latest, Published here, Put this site online, Undo this publish) and the earlier ones, all by Tobiah Rusk.
Put this site online, step 1 of 4, over the Online screen: Cloudflare (Recommended) or Vercel.
Use your own domain: www.caddow.example checked — Cloudflare will answer it with this site; nothing else on caddow.example changes.

Online after going live on the stand-in host: www.caddow.example (your own address) with its Copy button, On Cloudflare · project caddow, Editor online, and the deployment to caddow.example-studio.workers.dev.
Online after going live, with the Editor online section: edit this site from any browser, Host the editor online.

Host the editor online, step 5 of 5, Check the plan, against the stand-in Fly.io: what will be created (app, addresses, disk, computer, three certificates) and What it costs (up to about $13 a month; it sleeps while nobody is using it). Nothing is created.
A hosted install's sign-in (galley serve on this computer, a throwaway password): Sign in to edit, and that setting up isn't finished.

A hosted install's first run, step 2 Site: Connect the site — a repository that already holds the site or a starter, the repository address, and the editor's own key (a public key made by that throwaway install) or an access token. No site is connected.
Bring your WordPress site, steps 1–4, from the stand-in Fernhill Garden Studio into Lowfield.
Arrange on the home page: Lookbook grid 3/11 selected with its toolbar, its options and the section library.
Recording (muted, loops): a Newsletter section found in the library and dragged onto the home page under the campaign hero.

screens.shows: The docs pages' pictures, each at the exact size its page declares.

screens.step: the step named in each guide's comment in capture-screens.mjs
screens.shows: The how-to steps; their words, labels and alt text are in src/data/howto.json, written by the same steps.
The example site itself (not re-made for this set).

notes: The session: GA4, redirects, a form field, the brand and two Search & AI fixes are each published as Tobiah Rusk, so Version history reads as one session; then three changes wait in Proof (the atelier heading in the form, the Pieces heading on the page, the campaign hero and the journal heading by the assistant) for every showcase capture; then they are published, and the site goes online on the stand-in host. Then "Host the editor online" is walked to its plan against the stand-in Fly.io (nothing created), and a hosted install started on this computer is signed in to its first run (no site connected: a hosted install only takes a repository on a code host).

search-ai first publishes a journal post that still links to /about-us/ (now redirected), so Search & AI has a certain fix to offer. Its first run of the checks usually finds the preview's pages still compiling, so it runs them twice.

Inbox: the two visitors (Ines Marrow, Corin Vale) and the newsletter sign-up are invented, and posted to the capture address from another local address (http://localhost:8080), as a page served some other way would: from the app's own address the inbox marks a submission Test.

Where a docs page's declared frame is a little smaller than the window it shows (arrange, media-generate, publish-dialog, undo-publish-dialog, proof-what-changed), a slightly larger area of the same shape is cut and brought to the declared size. The docs' assistant reply is taken in a 746 px window so the assistant pane is as wide as the picture.
The dev server's toolbar is hidden in every capture, including the recording.
Agent files are not captures: the /ai-first/ page shows this site's own files, read at build time.
